title: She looked unproductive.
paragraphs:
She looked unproductive.
But heaven called her chosen.

Everyone else was moving.
She was still.
And somehow… she was the only one who got it right.
Because what if your “faithfulness” is actually your distraction?

What if the very thing you’re proud of…
is the reason you’re missing Jesus?
Martha was busy. Responsible. Serving. Necessary.

On the floor.
Doing nothing.
At least… that’s how it looked.
But heaven doesn’t measure the way we do.
Some of us hide behind activity.

We serve so we don’t have to surrender.
We lead so we don’t have to listen.
We perform so we don’t have to be exposed.

Because you can be in the same house as Jesus
and still feel far from Him.

You can sing, preach, post, serve, organize…
and still not sit at His feet.
In Gospel of Luke 10:39–42, Scripture says:
“She had a sister called Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet and listened to his teaching. But Martha was distracted with much serving…” (Luke 10:39–40)

Not sinful on the outside.
Not immoral.
Not rebellious.
“Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things, but one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen the good portion…” (Luke 10:41–42)

Not ten.
Not balance.
Not better time management.

You can be doing things for Jesus
and still not be with Jesus.
And performance cannot heal your soul.
Because she knew something Martha didn’t—yet.
That posture—at His feet—was not laziness.
“I don’t have what I need unless it comes from You.”
And that is where the Gospel begins.
We are all Martha before we become Mary.

We strive.
We prove.
We perform.
We try to earn what can only be received.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God” (Romans 3:23)

That includes the busy ones.
The serving ones.
The “good” ones.
Sin is not just what you do wrong.
It’s also trusting yourself instead of God.
And no amount of spiritual activity can save you.
He didn’t come to make you busier.
Jesus Christ lived the life you could not live—perfect, righteous, fully obedient.
Then He went to the cross…

Not for rebels only,
but for the distracted.

For the anxious.
For the overworked soul trying to prove worth.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)

On that cross, Jesus carried your sin.
Your pride.
Your self-reliance.
Your hidden exhaustion.
And three days later, He rose again.
Proving that the way back to God is not through performance…
“For by grace you have been saved through faith… not a result of works” (Ephesians 2:8–9)
So here’s the question that will not leave you alone:
Are you Martha… hiding in motion?
Because one is anxious and troubled.
The other has chosen what will never be taken away.

Repent—not just of sin that looks bad,
but of the pride that keeps you busy instead of broken.
Lay down the pressure to perform.
And come back to His feet.
Whisper it if you have to:

Not your version of Him.
Not religion.
And He will meet you there.
